items.name: Kajo Park (Yamagata Castle ruins)
items.kicker: Free · grounds to 22:00 · the stops inside close 16:00-16:30
items.body: The moated grounds of Yamagata Castle, free and open 5:00-22:00 from Apr 1 to Oct 31, with several free history stops clustered inside — the Mogami Yoshiaki Historical Museum, the octagonal Meiji-era Kyu-Saiseikan, and the reconstructed Otemon Yagura gate-tower. The grounds stay open into the evening; the stops inside do not, so an afternoon arrival gets the walk but not the interiors. The Yagura opens 9:30-16:00 in its Sept-Nov bracket and closes for the season after Nov 2; its interior is open to visitors, though stairs-only access isn't confirmed — worth checking ahead for anyone with limited mobility.

items.name: Bunshokan
items.kicker: Free · the most accessible culture stop in the city
items.body:
The former prefectural capitol, a Taisho-era building — and the one Yamagata city sight whose access is actually documented. Free, 9:00-16:30, with a wheelchair-only entrance and accessible parking at the rear of the building, 10 loaner wheelchairs, a stair lift and a multipurpose toilet. Worth prioritizing for the group's 2 low-mobility travelers.

Closed the 1st and 3rd Monday of each month. The former assembly chamber is closed for construction until the end of September 2026 — re-check before counting on seeing it.

items.name: Kyu-Saiseikan
items.body: A distinctive octagonal, 3-tier former Meiji-era hospital building inside Kajo Park — free, open 9:00-16:30 with no weekly closing day (it shuts only Dec 29-Jan 3), and off the beaten path since most visitors head straight for the castle grounds instead. The 16:30 close is what decides whether an arrival-day visit works at all.

items.name: Mogami Yoshiaki Historical Museum
items.body: Dedicated to the daimyo who actually built Yamagata Castle — small, free, and squarely on-theme for a culture/history-focused visit without appearing on generic top-10 lists. Open 9:00-17:00 with last admission at 16:30; closed Mondays (the following day when the Monday is a public holiday).

items.name: Risshaku-ji (Yamadera)
items.body:
A mountain temple complex climbing a cliff face above the Yamadera valley, reached by a direct Senzan Line train from Yamagata. Admission is {{fact:yamadera-admission-500-yen}}. No cable car or shortcut exists — the climb to the Godaido viewing platform is on foot, the whole way. Konponchudo, the main hall near the base, is a complete stop on its own for anyone who'd rather not attempt the stairs.

⚠ Hours are published seasonally — 8:00-16:00 April-September, 8:30-15:00 December-March — with no October bracket at all. Treat it as a mid-afternoon close and confirm on the day.

items.name: Ginzan Onsen
items.kicker: Gas-lit ryokan street · best before 11:00 or after evening lamp-lighting
items.body:
A Taisho-era wooden ryokan street along the Ginzan River, with the riverside "Waraku" foot bath and Shirogane Falls (22m) at its end.

The gas lamps are lit at dusk — ⚠ reckon on ≈17:00 in late October, though no exact time is published; ask at your ryokan. Midday is the most crowded window. Staying overnight pays off here: before roughly 7:00 the street is nearly empty, well ahead of the day-trip crowds.

items.name: Yamagata Marugoto-kan Beninokura
items.kicker: Free to browse · ≈10 min walk from the station
items.body: A restored Edo-era safflower (beniba) merchant's warehouse compound — genuinely local, easy walking distance from the station, and pairs naturally with lunch at Soba Sanbyakubou inside the same complex.

items.correction: Raised to ¥500 as of April 1, 2025 — many guides and aggregator sites still quote the old figure.

items.claim: A cable car or ropeway can take you partway up Yamadera.
items.correction: No mechanized assist exists anywhere on the mountain. The only way beyond the base is on foot, via roughly 1,015 stone steps.

items.claim: You can drive up and park in Ginzan Onsen itself.
items.correction: The town center is pedestrian-only regardless. Day-trip parking sits on Route 188 outside the village. A winter 2025-26 car/entry-ticket restriction ran through March 1, 2026, and a shorter autumn 2025 version ran just two November weekends — 2026 dates for either aren't announced yet, so re-check closer to the trip; route buses, delivery vehicles, and overnight guests' ryokan parking are exempt regardless.

items.claim: IC cards (Suica) work everywhere around Yamagata the way they do in Tokyo.
items.correction: The Hanagasa Bus onward from Ōishida is cash-only — the operator's own fare table states cash settlement only, no IC cards. ⚠ Multiple Japanese sources also report that JR Ōishida Station itself doesn't accept IC cards, but that half couldn't be confirmed against JR East. Carry cash for the whole leg.
